All kinds of shit can cause hair loss. But in most men it's inherited (so-called Male Pattern Baldness, or MPB)

There is one recessive, sex-linked gene that determines whether men will develop MPB, or as some call it, premature balding.

The fact that the gene is on the X-chromosome is why it is common in men, but rare in women.

A number of other genes influence such things as how soon and how fast it happens, and how far it extends.

The biggest single factor influencing how fast and how extensively MPB happens, though, is testosterone levels. The one positive thing about male pattern baldness that starts early is, it usually means the guy has high testosterone.

Because of their much lower (10x lower) testosterone levels, women who are unfortunate enough to have two copies of the MPB gene don't start balding until older ages, and show a much weaker and less extensive pattern of hair loss.

Female Pattern Baldness happens when women have two copies of the recessive male pattern hair loss gene (complex) combined with relatively high levels for a female of testosterone. They get the Friar Tuck look of guys who have male pattern baldness, but it happens as a thinning of hair on the top of the head rather than a receding like in men, until finally there are just wisps on top and you can see the scalp through them.

Autoimmune disease can cause it. They lose hair all over, even their eyebrows and eyelashes. It gets thinner and thinner until there are just wisps left, sometimes they go completely bald.

Stress can make follicles weaker so that hair comes loose more easily. It's likely it could accelerate the pattern of hair loss in men who have the MPB gene, or women who have FPB.
All baldness is likely a product of stress, diet, extraneous chemical exposure, and/or genetics to some varying degree. A bald female must be mentally ill though.
